text:
The strongest ground is the Statute of Frauds-style writing requirement: in most states, a debt already barred by limitations can be revived only by a signed writing, so the oral promise is unenforceable. Lack of consideration is weak because Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 makes a promise to pay a barred debt binding without new consideration. The "deadbeat" remark is a distractor that supplies no consideration and no duress, and the varying length of limitations periods doesn't change the analysis because the question stipulates the debt is already barred.

CONFIDENCE: 70
